markdown_content: ## Animation Editor Overview and Play Region Management This section covers the usage of the Animation Editor in Clo 2025.1, focusing on managing the play region and recording animations, including techniques for extending and clamping the play region to selected layers. To access animation features, open the Animation Editor from the toolbar under "Animation." Within the editor, users can select avatars and motions from the library, such as female idle animations, and record them. A key improvement involves managing the play region more efficiently: - The play region can be manually extended by entering a higher frame number (e.g., 500) to cover the desired animation length. - Users can select the entire play region or specific layers and right-click to "Clamp region to selected layers," ensuring the play region matches the animation content precisely. - Holding Shift allows selecting multiple layers to clamp the play region encompassing all selected animations. After adjusting the play region, recording can resume from the new endpoint, capturing the extended animation seamlessly. If multiple animation recordings exist on the timeline, they can be merged by selecting the respective layers, right-clicking, and choosing "Merge layer." This combines separate recordings into one continuous animation, which can then be played back in the editor. Real-time playback can be toggled in the configurations panel to view animations at actual speed, enhancing review accuracy. ## User Interface Improvements: Configuration Panel and Timeline Controls This section details updates to the Animation Editor interface, particularly regarding the configuration panel's visibility and timeline scaling for better user experience. Previously, the configuration panel occupied a fixed space on the side, potentially limiting workspace. Now, users can: - Hover over the dividing black line adjacent to the configuration panel. - Click and drag to reduce the panel's width, minimizing its footprint while retaining access. - Increase or decrease the timeline area size to view more or fewer frames comfortably. These adjustments allow users to customize their workspace, balancing visibility of animation timelines and configuration options without cluttering the interface. ## Light Render Animation: New Features and Workflow This section explains the new capability to animate lighting within Clo 2025.1, including dome light controls, keyframe management, and rendering requirements. Previously, users could animate various elements but lacked the ability to animate lighting properties dynamically. The update introduces: - The option to add light render animation, specifically by controlling dome light parameters such as intensity and angle. - Users can activate keyframes for lighting attributes at specific timeline points. - Auto keyframe mode facilitates easier animation by automatically setting keyframes when properties change. Example workflow: 1. Enable the dome light in the scene. 2. Add an active keyframe at the starting frame, setting initial intensity and angle. 3. Move along the timeline and adjust dome light parameters (e.g., intensity to 3, angle to 25), with auto keyframe enabled to record changes. 4. Return to earlier frames to reset values as needed. 5. Play back the animation to see dynamic lighting changes. Note: To view light animation effects properly, users must enter the render mode and render the sequence, as the viewport does not display these lighting changes in real time. ## Exporting Avatar Animations with GLTF Format This section covers the ability to export avatar animations, including joint movements and light animations, in the GLTF format for compatibility and sharing. Clo 2025.1 now supports exporting avatar animations using the GLTF file format, which preserves joint animation data and light animations (excluding render lights that existed previously). To export: - Go to File > Export > GLTF. - Save the current avatar animation, including all keyframed movements and lighting changes. This feature facilitates integration with other 3D applications and workflows, enhancing asset portability and reuse. --- These updates in Clo 2025.1 provide enhanced control over animation timing, user interface customization, lighting animation capabilities, and improved export options, significantly advancing the animation pipeline and user experience.
